tast-tests: shill_stability: ask Upstart for PID The logic we use for determining the shill PID is complicated and can be much more easily done by simply asking Upstart what it thinks the PID is. This also fixes a subtle race condition: if a previous job has recently re-started shill, shill may not have finished fork()/execve() yet, and so a 'pgrep shill' will not find it yet. We could try to hack around this by modifying the shill Upstart job to report 'started' later, but really this is just a fact of life of many Upstart services -- the 'started' state does not necessarily mean everything is fully "up and running." BUG=none TEST=run back to back with, e.g., network.ConfigureServiceForProfile TEST=hack this job to run shill.Safe{Stop,Start}() first Change-Id: I40ebbfbbbae19f0254a787614ca693d8c0405fbd Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1647537 Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Kirtika Ruchandani <kirtika@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org>

tast-tests: network.ConfigureServiceForProfile: grab check_ethernet lock This script stops/starts shill a few times, to reset state and to test that its own state remains across restart. This causes us to lose connectivity briefly, and it gives the recover_duts/check_ethernet.hook infrastructure a chance to start screwing us up. This is particularly problematic if it: * decides to start disabling/re-enabling USB ethernet at the wrong time, as that may prevent our Ethernet Service (that this test looks for) from showing up promptly; or * restarts shill, which will cause us to lose our D-Bus connection and time out Solution: hold the check_ethernet lock for the duration of this test. See also http://crrev.com/c/1637489, which improves the locking on the recover_duts side. Note: even with this lock usage, there is still potentially some ramp-up time after this test, where we are no longer holding the lock but may have brief connectivity loss (while Ethernet is getting re-configured). That's a problem for the next test though ;) Note: shill.Safe{Stop,Start}() utilize the old /run/lock/shill-start.lock properly, but unfortunately this is all pretty racy too, since: (*) check_ethernet.hook doesn't currently acquire the lock -- it only reads it -- so there's still a race window (*) even if shill has started (in the Upstart sense), it may not have finished configuring Ethernet; so check_ethernet.hook may again find the lock "open", but connectivity not in good shape yet This is a problem for another day, requiring total revamp/replacement/removal of shill-start.lock. Fortunately, 'autotest_pause_ethernet_hook' is a sufficient superset of that lock, and it satisfies the needs of this test. I also add the clean-profile-on-exit logic that is present in the Autotest version, but not the Tast version of this test. shill: make upstart job 'expect fork' It's nice if, when our Upstart job reaches the 'started' state, we can expect there to be a shill process on the system. This is particularly helpful for tests like Tast's network.ShillStability, which can run very quickly after a test that restarts shill. I noticed problems here when running tast run ${HOST} network.ConfigureServiceForProfile network.ShillStability This significantly tightens that race, but it doesn't completely resolve it -- there's a tiny window between when minijail0 forks and when it exec's shill. So 'started shill' may still briefly show only a minijail0 process. BUG=none TEST=`tast ... network.ShillStability`, modified to call shill.Safe{Stop,Start}() first (or, back to back with other tests that start/stop shill) Change-Id: I8d95e1211fa418c85451364e7cc41cbd8de9c57b Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1647315 Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Micah Morton <mortonm@chromium.org>

shill: stop forcing low bitrates during association/configuration This code was somewhere between a workaround and a real fix -- it's probably a better maintenance model to fix up a device's rate control algorithm, rather than specify exactly which rates it should use. For one, forcing low rates can directly conflict with some enterprise configurations, which explicitly try to steer clients toward only higher rates (to help budget airtime). Additionally, we can run into situations where the Basic Rates advertised by an AP don't overlap with the rates we've forced here (noticed to some extent in https://crbug.com/886529) -- and the result is that drivers tend to just ignore the request we're making here entirely. We've already fixed up the one driver that (we think) was driving the adoption of this feature in the first place (ath9k) to use a better rate control algorithm, so hopefully we're not losing out on anything. We may want to loosen up (or drop entirely) the network_WiFi_LowInitialBitrates Autotest, although to some extent it may still be valid: we expect drivers not to jump to extremely high bitrates too quickly, or else they may have reliability issues. BUG=chromium:947642 TEST=unit tests TEST=association on a variety of devices (esp. ath9k) Change-Id: Ia4b7c1de33c1c6eb3c2430a4e92f9c945332dd8f Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1626264 Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Neeraj Poojary <npoojary@chromium.org>
